A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Illustrator’s Depth research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and included supplementary sections are readable and support matching retained, revised, added, and relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original depth-prediction and vectorization experiments, ablations, SVGX evaluation, and qualitative application results in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and additionally reports WikiArt quantitative evaluation and nearest-neighbor analysis.

M1.justification: The proposed Depth Pro initialization, SVG curation, normalized layer-index MAE objective, and postprocessing pipelines are unchanged. The revised VTracer comparator and additional evaluation procedures do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Supplementary Section 15 adds evaluation on 1,000 random WikiArt artworks, substantially expanding the evaluated artwork corpus beyond v1’s selected qualitative examples. MMSVG, SVGX, training coverage, and the existing application tasks remain.

E2.justification: Section 4.2 and Table 3 replace standalone VTracer with VTracer combined with Potrace and matching cleanups. Other vectorization comparators remain unchanged. The new WikiArt comparison reuses Depth Pro and Depth Anything-v2, rather than introducing additional comparator families.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a quantitative artwork protocol using CLIP-I and DreamSim for depth-map/input similarity, plus MAE, MSE, and SSIM for RGB reconstructions after binning into 100 layers. It also matches the VTracer comparator’s tracing and cleanups to the proposed pipeline. Existing training budgets and SVG splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 16 and Figure 20 examine training/test similarity through RGB- and depth-based nearest neighbors for two test images. The artwork evaluation adds a reconstruction case study in Figure 19. Existing component ablations, inpainting comparisons, failure cases, and order-metric sensitivity analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same random-pair sampling description and order-metric stability analysis in Section 14 and Figure 18. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical significance procedures.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports WikiArt results, including SSIM 0.640 for Ours versus 0.387 for Depth Pro and 0.427 for Depth Anything-v2. Table 3 replaces the VTracer row: Order changes from 0.689 to 0.694 and path-count error from 3.65 to 0.83; SSIM and LPIPS now tie Ours. These are revised-comparator results, while existing proposed-method SVG scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The layer-index definition, rasterization encoding, normalization, loss, and ordering-consistency formulation are unchanged. The added empirical metrics and nearest-neighbor discussion introduce no formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about layer-index prediction, vectorization, layer-quality evaluation, text-to-vector generation, and editing applications. Added evaluations support existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 softens the explanation of generalization to pretrained priors being the most likely cause, and Section 4.4.2 states that the approach is not intended to rival segmentation models. New Section 15 explicitly acknowledges that perceptual and reconstruction scores cannot assess layer-index fidelity.

D1.justification: The supplementary introduction newly identifies interactive.html, mmsvg-100.html, and showcase.html and describes their contents. Those companion files are not supplied for verification. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, vectorization threshold, and generation prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for DreamSim, CLIPScore, and Instance Segmentation of Scene Sketches Using Natural Image Priors. The broader research positioning remains stable. NeuralSVG and LayerTracer receive publication updates rather than representing newly cited works.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the introduction and application discussion, an expanded supplementary overview, and two new supplementary sections. The existing narrative and section order are largely preserved; Additional Results moves from Section 15 to Section 17.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 and Figures 19–20, while retaining the earlier histogram and pop-up-card illustration as Figures 21–22. Existing figures and tables are repositioned or resized, with tighter pagination, but the overall visual structure remains similar.

improvement.justification: The matched VTracer+Potrace comparison strengthens experimental fairness, while the WikiArt evaluation and explicit qualifications improve support for the generalization discussion. These gains are limited: artwork proxies cannot establish correct layer ordering, and the two illustrated nearest-neighbor examples do not substantiate novelty of the entire test set. The core method and existing SVG results remain unchanged.
